method_note: Two measurement methods, chosen via --method (default 'auto'). 'diff': two identical non-streaming requests per rep that differ only in max_tokens (1 vs gen_tokens). tA_s/tB_s are their wall-clock latencies; ctA/ctB are usage.completion_tokens from each response; pt is usage.prompt_tokens from request A. ttft_s = tA_s -- NOT a pure prefill-only measurement: it includes prefill, one decode step, and request/response overhead. prefill_tok_s = pt / tA_s. decode_tok_s = (ctB - ctA) / (tB_s - tA_s), or null with decode_skipped='early_stop' if ctB - ctA < 16, or decode_skipped='server_ignores_max_tokens' instead if EVERY rep at that length had ctA == ctB (the server did not honor max_tokens=1, so decode speed cannot be inferred this way). e2e_s = tB_s. 'stream': one streaming (SSE) request per rep with max_tokens=gen_tokens. ttft_s = arrival time of the first chunk whose delta.content is non-empty. n_out = usage.completion_tokens if the server sends a final usage chunk (requested via stream_options.include_usage, retried once without it on HTTP 400), else the number of content chunks received (token_source records which). prefill_tok_s = pt / ttft_s, where pt is the PER-LENGTH prompt token count from that length's ordinary (non-streaming) calibration request -- not a per-rep value. decode_tok_s = (n_out - 1) / (t_last_chunk - t_first_chunk) when n_out >= 16 and that duration is positive, else null with a decode_skipped reason. e2e_s = wall-clock time to [DONE]/EOF. 'auto': calibrates the first length, then sends one streaming probe request (max_tokens=gen_tokens) at that length; uses 'stream' for the whole run if it yields >=4 content chunks, else 'diff'. The outcome is recorded as top-level 'method' and 'method_reason'. Calibration requests (finding a prompt whose token count is close to a length's target) are always non-streaming with max_tokens=1 and are excluded from all timing, in both methods -- if a server ignores max_tokens this only costs calibration time, not correctness. Per-length summary keys (ttft_s, prefill_tok_s, decode_tok_s, e2e_s as mean/std) have the same meaning and shape in both methods. If calibration fails for a length after the first, that length is recorded as {'target','error','reps':[]} and the run continues; the process exits 4 (no output file written) only if the FIRST length's calibration fails (server looks unusable); exits 5 (output file still written) if the file was written but at least one later length failed calibration; exits 0 if every length produced data.
